nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What materials were used to develop the supercapacitor mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The supercapacitor utilized biomass-derived carbon electrodes, specifically iodine- and sulphur-doped activated carbon (iodine@S-doped SPAC).
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Developing appropriate electrode materials is crucial for achieving supercapacitors with high power output and extended cycle life. Among these, biomass-derived carbon electrodes hold a prominent position in supercapacitor applications. How - ever, these electrodes need to be modified by appropriate methods to increase their performance. In this study, sulphur and iodine heteroatom functionalization was performed using a hydrothermal method on activated carbon (SPAC) derived from a microalgae precursor through potassium hydroxide activation, resulting in iodine- and sulphur-doped SPAC (iodine@S-doped SPAC). Characterization was carried out with Scanning electron microscope (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction analysis (XRD), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and nitrogen adsorption/desorption analyses. The electrochemical properties of the resulting composite material as a supercapacitor were examined. A specific capacitance of 208.95 F/g was achieved with the iodine@S-doped SPAC supercapacitor. The maximum energy density and power density of the supercapacitor, derived from the iodine@S-doped SPAC sample, were calculated as 5.11 Wh/kg and 2000 W/kg, respectively. Additionally, the coulombic efficiency of this supercapacitor was calculated to be 87.57% at a cur - rent density of 0.6 A/g.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the role of nitrogen atoms in heteroatom doping of carbon materials for supercapacitors?
nodes.answer: Nitrogen atoms enhance electron conductivity and improve pseudocapacitance through Faradaic reactions in carbon materials.
nodes.paragraph: In supercapacitor applications, car - bon edges are modified through heteroatom doping, which enhances electron conductivity and improves pseudocapaci- tance via Faradaic reactions [19 21]. The use of N atoms with high electronegativity has been frequently reported in heteroatom-doping applications to carbon materials [22, 23]. Sulphur, which has a larger radius and higher electro- chemical activity compared to nitrogen, is added to carbo- naceous materials as a heteroatom, disrupting the electron balance density of the material and resulting in different bond lengths and bond angles [1 , 24]. Sulphur-doped car - bon materials also have significant interest in supercapacitor applications. Another important element among heteroatoms is iodine. The iodine doping has begun to be considered especially in some applications [ 25 27]. There is still little research on iodine doping into porous carbon structure. With iodine atoms having a relatively high electronegativity (2.66) and a larger radius (140 pm) compared to carbon, both the elec- tronic structure of carbon materials can be optimized and the d-spacing can be increased [28]. Thus, we believe that investigating how iodine can be integrated into carbon mate- rials to enhance energy storage performance in supercapaci- tor applications is of great importance.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the study discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main focus of the study is the synthesis of iodine@S-doped SPAC using Spirulina platensis as the carbon precursor for electrode material in supercapacitor applications.
nodes.paragraph: Doping iodine as a heteroatom can significantly increase the electrochemically active sites of carbon-based materials [29, 30]. Biomass-based carbon materials are widely used in vari- ous application areas [31 33]. Among biomass-based car - bon materials, algae have attracted great attention in differ - ent application areas with their important features such as fast growth rates and high photosynthetic efficiency [ 34]. Spirulina platensis, which has an important place among algae and is characterized by rapid growth and wide distribu- tion, consists mainly of polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids. One of the significant properties of Spirulina platensis is its natural nitrogen content. Therefore, it can be utilized in various applications without requiring an additional nitrogen source for doping. With its low cost and these advantageous characteristics, Spirulina platensis emerges as a promising candidate for biomass-derived carbon materials as electrodes in supercapacitor applications. This study focuses on the synthesis of iodine@S-doped SPAC through a series of pyrolysis and hydrothermal processes, utilizing Spirulina platensis microalgae as the carbon precursor, with S and I atoms as heteroatoms for electrode material in supercapaci- tor applications.

The high specific capacitance, electrical conductivity, and electro - chemical stability of metal oxides have made them one of the most suitable candidates for supercapacitor doping [ 1]. Metal oxides can store a large amount of charge per volume or mass, which is important for supercapacitor applications. Co3O4 has attracted the attention of researchers with its high specific capacitance, higher energy density than carbon materials, more stable structure than conducting polymers, and lower cost [ 2 4].

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What materials were used to prepare the RF xerogel electrodes in the study?
nodes.answer: The materials used were resorcinol, cobalt nitrate, formaldehyde, and sodium carbonate.
nodes.paragraph: In this study, RF xerogel electrodes doped with Co3O4 at four different doping ratios (25, 50, 75, 100%) were pre - pared, and their supercapacitor performances were studied. The structural properties of the prepared electrodes were analyzed by XRD and FTIR, their surface morphology by FESEM, and their compositional analysis by EDX. Elec - trochemical characterizations were performed, the specific capacitance, energy, and power densities of each superca - pacitor were determined, and the effects of Co3O4 doping on the performance of the xerogels were compared. 2 Experimental section 2.1 Preparation of Co3O4 doped RF xerogel To prepare supercapacitor electrode active materials, four separate beakers were used to prepare resorcinol-cobalt mixtures with different ratios of Co O doping. 0.625 g of resorcinol was dissolved in about 10 mL of pure water in 4 different beakers. 25 50% 75 100% cobalt nitrate was added to these solutions. After the mixtures became homo - geneous, 0.9 g of 37% formaldehyde was added. Then, 0.3 g sodium carbonate was added to the solutions. Sodium carbonate is a slightly basic compound that helps control the pH of the reaction medium.

nodes.question: How were the electrical charge characteristics of REEs/C measured?
nodes.answer: The electrical charge characteristics of REEs/C were measured using a Zeta point position analyser in different pH levels (NANO ZS, Malvern Panalytical, UK).
nodes.paragraph: The specific surface areas of Dicranopteris pedata REEs/C with different preparation temperatures were obtained from Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET, BELSORP-mini II, Japan), based on N2 adsorption and desorption curves. The morphological and elemental compositions of Dicranopteris pedata REEs/C with different preparation temperatures were detected by Ultrahigh resolution cold field emission scanning electron microscope (SEM, Regulus 8100, Hitachi, JPN). It was combined with EDS (JEM-2100, Lorentz) using an acceleration voltage of 5.2 kV . Differences on the surface elemental composition and speciation of Dicranopteris pedata REEs/C with different preparation temperatures were analysed by Multifunctional imaging electron spectrometer (XPS, Thermo ESCALAB 250XI, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). Here the test parameters were ALK (hv = 1486.6 eV), 150 W 500 m, and the calibration point of the binding energy of the instrument was C1s = 284.8 eV . The electrical charge characteristics of REEs/C with different preparation temperatures were measured using a Zeta point position analyser in different pH (NANO ZS, Malvern Panalytical, UK).
